# Core Mechanics {#core-mechanics}

Tomb Dust is a hardcore extraction fantasy roleplaying game set in the unforgiving world of Aventhar. Death is frequent; players should expect their characters to face overwhelming odds and often perish. The game celebrates the journey of each character, no matter how brief, and encourages players to learn from defeat. Striving to surpass previous accomplishments is an integral part of the Tomb Dust experience. In this brutal world, even small victories are meaningful, and legendary status is reserved for the truly exceptional and lucky few. For you are naught but… TOMB DUST\!

### 

## Tomb Dust Attribute System

Strength (STR): Physical power, affects melee damage and carrying capacity.  
Agility (AGI): Speed, reflexes, accuracy in combat, and evasion.  
Stamina (STA): Health, endurance, resistance to physical damage.  
Intellect (INT): Knowledge, reasoning, spell potency.  
Spirit (SPI): Willpower, magical resistance, regeneration of health and mana.  
Luck (LUC): 

## Attribute Impact on Gameplay

Evasion Check:

pythonCopyevasion\_roll \= random.randint(1, 100\)  
if evasion\_roll \<= target.derived\_stats\["evasion"\]:  
    \# Attack is evaded  
The evasion check works as follows:

A random number between 1 and 100 is rolled.  
If this number is less than or equal to the target's evasion stat, the attack is evaded.  
The evasion stat represents the percentage chance of avoiding an attack entirely.

For example, if a character has 20 evasion, they have a 20% chance to completely avoid any incoming attack.

Hit Check:

pythonCopyhit\_chance \= self.derived\_stats\["accuracy"\] \- target.derived\_stats\["evasion"\] \+ 50  
hit\_roll \= random.randint(1, 100\)  
if hit\_roll \> hit\_chance:  
    \# Attack misses  
The hit check is more complex:

It starts with the attacker's accuracy stat.  
It subtracts the target's evasion stat.  
It adds 50 to create a baseline hit chance.  
A random number between 1 and 100 is rolled.  
If this number is greater than the calculated hit chance, the attack misses.

This system works as follows:

The base 50 gives a 50% hit chance if accuracy and evasion are equal.  
Higher accuracy increases hit chance, while higher evasion decreases it.  
The final percentage is the likelihood of the attack hitting.

For example:

If the attacker has 70 accuracy and the target has 30 evasion:

Hit chance \= 70 \- 30 \+ 50 \= 90  
This means the attack has a 90% chance to hit

If the attacker has 40 accuracy and the target has 60 evasion:

Hit chance \= 40 \- 60 \+ 50 \= 30  
This means the attack has only a 30% chance to hit

Strength (STR)  
Melee Damage: Adds STR score to melee weapon damage.  
Carrying Capacity: STR x 10 units.  
Physical Tasks: Check: 1d12 \+ STR vs. difficulty.

Agility (AGI)  
Movement Points (MP): AGI score determines grid spaces moved per turn.  
Evasion: Base evasion score (10) \+ AGI.  
Accuracy: Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ AGI vs. target’s evasion score.

Stamina (STA)  
Health Points (HP): Base HP \+ (STA x 5).  
Endurance: Resists fatigue and physical damage. Check: 1d12 \+ STA vs. difficulty.  
Physical Resistance: Base physical defense (10) \+ STA.

Intellect (INT)  
Mana Points (MP): Base MP \+ (INT x 3).  
Spell Potency: Spell Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ INT vs. target’s magical defense.  
Knowledge Tasks: Check: 1d12 \+ INT vs. difficulty.

Spirit (SPI)  
Mana Regeneration: SPI score determines MP recovered per turn.  
Resilience: Base magical defense (10) \+ SPI.  
Healing Rate: Additional HP recovered per rest period, equal to SPI score.  
Willpower: Check: 1d12 \+ SPI vs. fear or mental attack difficulty.

## Combat Calculations

Magical Attack Score  
Formula: (Base Score \+ INT \+ Skill/Equipment Bonuses) / 2  
Example: (10 \+ 5 \+ 2\) / 2 \= 8.5 (rounded down to 8\)

Melee Attack Score  
Formula: (Base Score \+ STR \+ Skill/Equipment Bonuses) / 2  
Example: (10 \+ 5 \+ 2\) / 2 \= 8

Ranged Attack Score  
Formula: (Base Score \+ AGI \+ Skill/Equipment Bonuses) / 2  
Example: (10 \+ 6 \+ 3\) / 2 \= 9

Physical Defense  
Formula: Base Score \+ STA \+ AGI  
Example: 10 \+ 7 \+ 5 \= 22

Magical Defense  
Formula: Base Score \+ SPI  
Example: 10 \+ 5 \= 15

Combat Interaction Example  
Attacker’s Melee Attack: 1d12 \+ 8 vs. Physical Defense (22)  
Attacker’s Ranged Attack: 1d12 \+ 9 vs. Physical Defense (22)  
Magical Attack vs. Magical Defense: 1d12 \+ Magical Attack Score vs. 10 \+ SPI

## Creating a character and determining base scores {#creating-a-character-and-determining-base-scores}

Playable Races \- select a race\!

1\. \*\*Humans\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+1 to any two attributes of the player's choice.  
   \- Description: Adaptable and versatile, humans thrive in various environments and possess a remarkable capacity for learning and mastering multiple disciplines.

2\. \*\*High Elves\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 INT, \+1 AGI  
   \- Description: Graceful and wise, high elves live in harmony with the natural magic of Aventhar, excelling in arcane arts and knowledge.

3\. \*\*Dark Elves\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 AGI, \+1 INT, \-1 SPI  
   \- Description: Embracing the teachings of Thar, dark elves reside in the underworld's depths, mastering dark magic and craftsmanship.

4\. \*\*Wood Elves\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 AGI, \+1 SPI  
   \- Description: Masters of the forests, wood elves are agile and deeply connected to nature, excelling in archery and natural magic.

5\. \*\*Dwarves\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 STA, \+1 STR, \-1 AGI  
   \- Description: Masters of craftsmanship and mining, dwarves are known for their resilience, honor, and loyalty, defending their deep mountain homes.

6\. \*\*Halflings\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 AGI, \+1 SPI  
   \- Description: Halflings are small but resilient, living in harmony with nature and embodying the essence of contentment and courage.

7\. \*\*Centaurs\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 STR, \+1 AGI, \-1 INT  
   \- Description: Roaming the plains and forests, centaurs are protectors of nature, renowned for their speed, strength, and wisdom.

8\. \*\*Aquarids\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 AGI, \+1 SPI, \-1 STA  
   \- Description: Humanoid beings from the deep seas, Aquarids excel in swimming, communication with sea creatures, and water manipulation.

9\. \*\*Demonkin\*\*  
   \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 SPI, \+1 STR, \-1 AGI  
   \- Description: Born from Thar's essence, demonkin are adept in dark magic, often driven by the desire to extend their influence and escape their infernal masters.

10\. \*\*Orcs\*\*  
    \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 STR, \+1 STA, \-1 INT  
    \- Description: Strong and fierce warriors from rugged lands, orcs excel in combat and survival, embodying brute strength and resilience.

11\. \*\*Gnomes\*\*  
    \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 INT, \+1 AGI, \-1 STR  
    \- Description: Inventive and quick-witted, gnomes are known for their ingenuity and dexterity, often excelling in technology and arcane studies.

12\. \*\*Dragonkin\*\*  
    \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 STR, \+1 SPI, \-1 AGI  
    \- Description: Bearing the blood of dragons, dragonkin are powerful and resilient, with a natural affinity for elemental magic.

13\. \*\*Faeries\*\*  
    \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 AGI, \+1 INT, \-1 STR  
    \- Description: Small and magical, faeries are known for their agility and trickery, often using their magical abilities to outwit larger foes.

14\. \*\*Minotaurs\*\*  
    \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 STR, \+1 STA, \-1 INT  
    \- Description: Powerful and imposing, minotaurs are known for their strength and endurance, often excelling as warriors and protectors.

15\. \*\*Undead\*\*  
    \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 SPI, \+1 STA, \-1 AGI  
    \- Description: Raised from the dead, undead are resilient to physical damage and possess a strong will, often excelling in necromantic arts.

16\. \*\*Trolls\*\*  
    \- Attribute Adjustments: \+2 STR, \+1 AGI, \-1 INT  
    \- Description: Tall and strong, trolls are known for their regenerative abilities and combat prowess, often excelling as fierce warriors and hunters.

## Base Rolls

1\. \*\*Base Attribute Roll\*\*  
   \- Roll 1d10 for each attribute to determine the initial base score.

2\. \*\*Genetic Factors\*\*  
   \- Roll 1d4 for each attribute to determine a genetic modifier (-1 to \+2). Refer to the Genetic Factors Table.

3\. \*\*Life Events\*\*  
   \- Roll 2d20 to determine a significant life event that impacts attributes. Refer to the Life Events Table for modifiers.

4\. \*\*Racial Adjustments\*\*  
   \- Apply the racial adjustments to the final base scores. Refer to the race list above and use the scores from the race you selected.

5\. \*\*Final Calculation\*\*  
   \- Combine the base roll, genetic factors, life event modifiers, and racial adjustments to determine final base scores for each attribute.

\*\*Example Calculation\*\*

\- \*\*Rolls for Attributes\*\*:   
  \- STR: 6   
  \- AGI: 5   
  \- STA: 4   
  \- INT: 7   
  \- SPI: 3

\- \*\*Genetic Factors\*\*:   
  \- STR \+2  
  \- AGI 0  
  \- STA \+1  
  \- INT \-1  
  \- SPI \+2

\- \*\*Life Event\*\*: Roll of 9 (Scholarly Pursuits: \+2 INT, \+1 SPI)

\- \*\*Race\*\*: High Elf (INT \+2, AGI \+1)

\- \*\*Final Base Scores\*\*:   
  \- STR: 8   
  \- AGI: 6   
  \- STA: 5   
  \- INT: 10   
  \- SPI: 6

# Class System {#class-system}

"Tomb Dust" is a brutal game where characters start as ordinary, struggling individuals, facing an unforgiving world. The class system is based on the character's life and progression. Most characters begin as peasants, farmers, servants, beggars, slaves, or street urchins. As they survive and progress, they can evolve into more advanced classes.

## Skills {#skills}

| Skill Level | Skill XP Required for Next Level | Total Skill XP Required | Gold Cost |  
|-------------|----------------------------------|-------------------------|----------------------------------|  
| Level 1     | 10 XP                            | 10 XP                   | 0                        |  
| Level 2     | 20 XP                            | 30 XP                   | 0                        |  
| Level 3     | 30 XP                            | 60 XP                   | 0                        |  
| Level 4     | 50 XP                            | 110 XP                  | 0                        |  
| Level 5     | 70 XP                            | 180 XP                  | 0                        |  
| Level 6     | 120 XP                           | 300 XP                  | 50 Gold                  |  
| Level 7     | 180 XP                           | 480 XP                  | 100 Gold                 |  
| Level 8     | 250 XP                           | 730 XP                  | 200 Gold                 |  
| Level 9     | 330 XP                           | 1060 XP                 | 400 Gold                 |  
| Level 10    | 420 XP                           | 1480 XP                 | 800 Gold                 |

## Skill Check System

Skill Check Formula: 2d6 \+ Skill Level vs. Difficulty Class (DC).  
Difficulty Class (DC): Set by the GM based on task difficulty.

Determining Difficulty Class (DC)  
The GM can set DCs to match the intended difficulty of tasks based on the typical skill levels characters might have. Here are some example DC ranges:

Easy (7-9): Tasks that a novice (Skill Level 1-3) has a fair chance of succeeding at.  
Medium (10-12): Tasks that require some proficiency (Skill Level 3-6) to succeed consistently.  
Hard (13-15): Tasks that challenge even experienced characters (Skill Level 5-8).  
Very Hard (16-18): Tasks that require near-mastery (Skill Level 7-10).  
Extreme (19+): Tasks that only true masters (Skill Level 9-10) can reliably succeed at.

Example Skill XP Gain Scenarios  
Scenario 1: Thalia the Rogue picks a simple lock (Easy Task, DC 8\)

Skill: Lockpicking  
Skill Level: 2  
AGI Score: 7  
Skill Check Calculation:  
Roll 2d6. Example: 4 and 5\.  
Total Roll: 4 \+ 5 \+ 2 (Skill Level) \+ 3 (AGI / 2\) \= 14  
DC: 8  
Result: Success (14 \> 8\)  
XP Gained: 1 Skill XP  
Summary  
Each successful skill check grants 1 Skill XP when the task difficulty is level appropriate or above.

Skill level 1 \- 3 | DC 7 \- 9  
Skill level 3 \- 6 | DC 10 \- 12  
Skill level 5 \- 8 | DC 13 \- 15  
Skill level 7 \- 10 | DC 16 \- 18  
Skill level 9 \- 10 | DC 19+

For example, if your lockpicking skill is level 4 and you successfully pick a lock with a DC of 7 you do NOT get a skill xp award for lockpicking. You would need to pick a lock with a DC of 10 or greater to earn skill xp.

Players accumulate Skill XP to advance their skill levels, adhering to the XP requirements table.  
Gold is required for advancement beyond level 5\.

## Combat Skills {#combat-skills}

1\. Swordsmanship (STR):  
Description: Proficiency with all types of swords.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and damage with swords.  
\- At levels 3, 6, and 9, unlock special sword techniques.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Swordsmanship \+ (STR / 2\)  
Damage: Sword Damage \+ STR \+ Swordsmanship

Special Techniques:  
Level 3: Precision Strike \- Ignore 2 points of target's physical defense  
Level 6: Whirlwind Attack \- Attack all adjacent enemies with a \-2 penalty  
Level 9: Vital Strike \- On a critical hit, double the Swordsmanship bonus to damage

2\. Axe Mastery (STR):  
Description: Skill with axes and hatchets.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and damage with axes.  
\- Increases chance for devastating cleaving attacks.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Axe Mastery \+ (STR / 2\)  
Damage: Axe Damage \+ STR \+ Axe Mastery  
Cleave Chance: 10% \+ (5% x Axe Mastery level)

Special:  
On a successful hit, roll percentile dice. If roll ≤ Cleave Chance, the attack also hits an adjacent enemy for half damage.

Progression:  
Level 3: Unlock "Rending Strike" \- Ignores 25% of target's armor  
Level 6: Unlock "Crushing Blow" \- 50% chance to stun target for 1 round  
Level 9: Unlock "Berserker Fury" \- Make an additional attack at \-2 penalty

3\. Mace and Flail Expertise (STR):  
Description: Ability to wield blunt weapons effectively.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and damage with maces and flails.  
\- Increases chance to stun opponents.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Mace and Flail Expertise \+ (STR / 2\)  
Damage: Weapon Damage \+ STR \+ Mace and Flail Expertise  
Stun Chance: 5% \+ (3% x Mace and Flail Expertise level)

Special:  
On a successful hit, roll percentile dice. If roll ≤ Stun Chance, the target is stunned for 1 round.

Progression:  
Level 3: Unlock "Bone Crusher" \- Ignore 2 points of target's physical defense  
Level 6: Unlock "Daze" \- On a critical hit, target is dazed (-2 to all actions) for 2 rounds  
Level 9: Unlock "Flail Mastery" \- Attacks with flails ignore shield bonuses

4\. Polearm Proficiency (STR):  
Description: Skill with spears, halberds, and pikes.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and damage with polearms.  
\- Improves reach and defensive capabilities.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Polearm Proficiency \+ (STR / 2\)  
Damage: Polearm Damage \+ STR \+ Polearm Proficiency  
Defensive Bonus: \+1 to Physical Defense when wielding a polearm

Special:  
Can attack enemies 2 squares away instead of just adjacent squares.

Progression:  
Level 3: Unlock "Thrust" \- Attack ignores 2 points of target's physical defense  
Level 6: Unlock "Sweep" \- Attack all enemies in a 180-degree arc in front of you at \-2 penalty  
Level 9: Unlock "Set Against Charge" \- Double damage against charging enemies

5\. Archery (AGI):  
Description: Skill with all types of bows.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and \+1 to damage with bows.  
\- Increases effective range of bow attacks.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Archery \+ (AGI / 2\)  
Damage: Arrow Damage \+ (AGI / 2\) \+ Archery  
Range Increase: Base range \+ (10% x Archery level)

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Precise Shot" \- Ignore cover bonuses to target's defense  
Level 6: Unlock "Rapid Shot" \- Fire two arrows in one action at \-2 penalty each  
Level 9: Unlock "Penetrating Shot" \- Arrow can hit two targets in a line

6\. Crossbow Expertise (AGI):  
Description: Proficiency with crossbows.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and \+2 to damage with crossbows.  
\- Improves reload speed and armor penetration.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Crossbow Expertise \+ (AGI / 2\)  
Damage: Bolt Damage \+ Crossbow Expertise x 2  
Armor Penetration: Ignore 1 point of target's physical defense per 2 levels of Crossbow Expertise

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Quick Load" \- Reduce reload time by 1 action  
Level 6: Unlock "Piercing Bolt" \- Ignore half of target's armor  
Level 9: Unlock "Multi-Shot" \- Fire 3 bolts in a spread, each at \-2 penalty

7\. Throwing Weapons (AGI):  
Description: Skill with daggers, axes, and other thrown implements.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and damage with thrown weapons.  
\- Increases range and allows for multiple throws per round at higher levels.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Throwing Weapons \+ (AGI / 2\)  
Damage: Weapon Damage \+ (AGI / 2\) \+ Throwing Weapons  
Range Increase: Base range \+ (15% x Throwing Weapons level)

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Quick Draw" \- Draw and throw as a single action  
Level 6: Unlock "Dual Throw" \- Throw two weapons in one action at \-2 penalty each  
Level 9: Unlock "Return Throw" \- 50% chance for thrown weapon to return to hand

8\. Unarmed Combat (STR):  
Description: Skill in fighting without weapons.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and damage with unarmed attacks.  
\- Improves grappling ability.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Unarmed Combat \+ (STR / 2\)  
Damage: 1d4 \+ STR \+ Unarmed Combat  
Grapple Check: 1d12 \+ Unarmed Combat \+ STR vs. opponent's 1d12 \+ Unarmed Combat/Athletics \+ STR

Special:  
Level 3: Unarmed damage die increases to 1d6  
Level 6: Unlock "Stunning Fist" \- 50% chance to stun target for 1 round on a critical hit  
Level 9: Unarmed damage die increases to 1d8

9\. Martial Arts (AGI):  
Description: Advanced unarmed combat techniques.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides \+1 to hit and damage with unarmed attacks.  
\- Unlocks special combat maneuvers.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Martial Arts \+ (AGI / 2\)  
Damage: 1d4 \+ STR \+ Martial Arts

Special:  
Level 2: Unarmed damage die increases to 1d6  
Level 4: Unlock "Disabling Strike" \- 50% chance to reduce target's AGI by 2 for 2 rounds  
Level 6: Unarmed damage die increases to 1d8  
Level 8: Unlock "Flowing Strikes" \- Make an additional unarmed attack on a critical hit  
Level 10: Unarmed damage die increases to 1d10

10\. Shield Use (STR):  
Description: Ability to effectively use shields.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level increases chance to block and reduces damage from blocked attacks.

Formula:  
Block Chance: 20% \+ (5% x Shield Use level)  
Damage Reduction: 1 \+ Shield Use level

Special:  
When an attack is successfully blocked, reduce the incoming damage by the Damage Reduction value.

Level 5: Unlock "Shield Bash" \- Use shield as an off-hand weapon  
Level 8: Unlock "Deflection" \- Once per combat, automatically block one attack  
Level 10: Unlock "Phalanx" \- Grant adjacent allies \+2 to Physical Defense

11\. Dodge (AGI):  
Description: Skill at avoiding attacks.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a cumulative 5% chance to completely avoid an attack.  
\- This is rolled after a successful hit is determined.

Formula:  
Dodge Chance: 5% x Dodge Skill Level  
Dodge Roll: 1d100 ≤ Dodge Chance

Special:  
Level 5: Unlock "Evasion" \- Half damage from area effects on a successful dodge  
Level 8: Unlock "Uncanny Dodge" \- Cannot be caught flat-footed  
Level 10: Unlock "Superior Evasion" \- No damage from area effects on a successful dodge

12\. Armor Proficiency (STA):  
Description: Ability to move and fight effectively in armor.  
Mechanics:  
\- Reduces penalties from wearing heavier armor.  
\- Improves overall defense when wearing armor.

Formula:  
Armor Penalty Reduction: \-1 per 2 levels of Armor Proficiency  
Defense Bonus: \+1 to Physical Defense per 3 levels of Armor Proficiency when wearing armor

Special:  
Level 5: Unlock "Second Skin" \- Reduce armor check penalty by half  
Level 8: Unlock "Indomitable" \- Once per day, ignore a critical hit (treat as normal hit)  
Level 10: Unlock "Living Fortress" \- Reduce all incoming physical damage by 2 when wearing heavy armor

13\. Dual Wielding (AGI):  
Description: Skill at fighting with a weapon in each hand.  
Mechanics:  
\- Reduces penalties for fighting with two weapons.  
\- Improves damage output when dual wielding.

Formula:  
Main Hand Attack: 1d12 \+ Dual Wielding \+ (AGI / 2\)  
Off Hand Attack: 1d12 \+ (Dual Wielding / 2\) \+ (AGI / 2\)  
Off Hand Damage Bonus: \+(Dual Wielding / 2\)

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Flurry" \- Once per combat, make an additional off-hand attack  
Level 6: Unlock "Balanced Grip" \- Off-hand attacks use full Dual Wielding bonus  
Level 9: Unlock "Whirlwind Strike" \- Attack all adjacent enemies once with each weapon

14\. Battlefield Awareness (INT):  
Description: Understanding of overall combat situations.  
Mechanics:  
\- Provides bonus to initiative rolls.  
\- Allows for better positioning in combat.

Formula:  
Initiative Bonus: \+1 per 2 levels of Battlefield Awareness (rounded down)  
Positioning Check: 1d12 \+ Battlefield Awareness \+ (INT / 2\) vs. DC

Special:  
At levels 5 and 10, the character can reposition one ally as a free action once per combat.

15\. Power Attack (STR):  
Description: Ability to trade accuracy for increased damage in melee combat.  
Mechanics:  
\- For every \-1 penalty to the attack roll, the character gains a \+2 bonus to damage.  
\- The maximum penalty/bonus is equal to the character's Power Attack skill level.  
\- This decision must be made before the attack roll.

Formula:  
Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Weapon Skill \+ (STR / 2\) \- Power Attack Penalty  
Damage: Weapon Damage \+ STR \+ (Power Attack Penalty x 2\)

Skill Progression:  
Level 1: Can use Power Attack with a max \-1 penalty/+2 damage  
Level 3: Max \-3 penalty/+6 damage  
Level 5: Max \-5 penalty/+10 damage  
Level 7: Max \-7 penalty/+14 damage  
Level 10: Max \-10 penalty/+20 damage

Certainly\! Let's move on to the next category of skills: Physical Skills. We'll apply the same level of detail as we did with the combat skills.

## Physical Skills: {#physical-skills:}

1\. Athletics (STR):  
Description: General physical fitness, running, jumping, and climbing.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to physical feats.  
\- Improves movement speed and carrying capacity.

Formula:  
Athletic Check: 1d12 \+ Athletics \+ (STR / 2\) vs. DC  
Movement Speed Bonus: \+5% per 2 levels of Athletics  
Carrying Capacity Bonus: \+5% per level of Athletics

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Burst of Speed" \- Once per day, double movement speed for 1 round  
Level 6: Unlock "Mighty Leap" \- Add Athletics level to jump distance/height  
Level 9: Unlock "Peak Performance" \- Once per day, automatically succeed on an Athletics check

2\. Acrobatics (AGI):  
Description: Balance, tumbling, and agile maneuvers.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to acrobatic feats.  
\- Reduces falling damage and improves ability to move through difficult terrain.

Formula:  
Acrobatic Check: 1d12 \+ Acrobatics \+ (AGI / 2\) vs. DC  
Falling Damage Reduction: Reduce falling damage by 1d6 per 2 levels of Acrobatics

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Tumble" \- Move through enemy-occupied spaces without provoking attacks of opportunity  
Level 6: Unlock "Cat's Grace" \- Always land on your feet when falling  
Level 9: Unlock "Impossible Dodge" \- Once per day, automatically succeed on a Dodge roll

3\. Stealth (AGI):  
Description: Moving silently and remaining unseen.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to stealth checks.  
\- Improves ability to hide and move undetected.

Formula:  
Stealth Check: 1d12 \+ Stealth \+ (AGI / 2\) vs. Perception DC  
Movement while Stealthing: 50% normal speed \+ 5% per level of Stealth (max 100%)

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Shadow Blend" \- Gain advantage on Stealth checks in dim light or darkness  
Level 6: Unlock "Silent Step" \- No movement penalty to Stealth checks  
Level 9: Unlock "Vanish" \- Once per day, become invisible for 1d4 rounds

4\. Sleight of Hand (AGI):  
Description: Manual dexterity for fine manipulation and pickpocketing.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Sleight of Hand checks.  
\- Improves ability to conceal small objects and pick pockets.

Formula:  
Sleight of Hand Check: 1d12 \+ Sleight of Hand \+ (AGI / 2\) vs. Perception DC  
Pickpocket Value: Can steal items worth up to (5 gold x Sleight of Hand level) without penalty

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Fast Hands" \- Perform Sleight of Hand checks as a free action once per round  
Level 6: Unlock "Misdirection" \- Gain advantage on Sleight of Hand checks when you have a distraction  
Level 9: Unlock "Perfect Theft" \- Once per day, automatically succeed on a Sleight of Hand check

5\. Endurance (STA):  
Description: Ability to withstand physical strain and fatigue.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Endurance checks.  
\- Improves resistance to fatigue and environmental hazards.

Formula:  
Endurance Check: 1d12 \+ Endurance \+ (STA / 2\) vs. DC  
Fatigue Resistance: Extend time before fatigue sets in by 10% per Endurance level

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Second Wind" \- Once per day, recover 2d6 HP as a free action  
Level 6: Unlock "Iron Stomach" \- Advantage on checks to resist poison and disease  
Level 9: Unlock "Tireless" \- Ignore the effects of fatigue for 1 hour per day

Certainly\! Let's move on to the Social Skills category. We'll maintain the same level of detail as with the previous categories.

## Social Skills:

1\. Persuasion (SPI):  
Description: Convincing others through argument or charm.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Persuasion checks.  
\- Improves ability to change attitudes and negotiate.

Formula:  
Persuasion Check: 1d12 \+ Persuasion \+ (SPI / 2\) vs. Target's Willpower DC  
Attitude Improvement: Can improve target's attitude by one step per 3 levels of Persuasion

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Silver Tongue" \- Reroll one failed Persuasion check per day  
Level 6: Unlock "Compelling Argument" \- Target has disadvantage on Willpower saves against your Persuasion  
Level 9: Unlock "Mass Appeal" \- Persuasion checks can affect a group of up to Persuasion level individuals

2\. Intimidation (STR or SPI, whichever is higher):  
Description: Coercing others through fear or threats.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Intimidation checks.  
\- Improves ability to frighten or coerce targets.

Formula:  
Intimidation Check: 1d12 \+ Intimidation \+ (STR or SPI / 2\) vs. Target's Willpower DC  
Fear Duration: Successful intimidation lasts for 1 round per Intimidation level

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Frightening Presence" \- Intimidate all enemies within 30 feet as a single action  
Level 6: Unlock "Breaking Point" \- On a critical success, target becomes friendly for 1d4 hours out of fear  
Level 9: Unlock "Terrifying Aura" \- Enemies within 10 feet have disadvantage on attacks against you

3\. Deception (INT):  
Description: Lying convincingly and misdirection.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Deception checks.  
\- Improves ability to craft and maintain lies.

Formula:  
Deception Check: 1d12 \+ Deception \+ (INT / 2\) vs. Target's Insight DC  
Lie Complexity: Can maintain lies with (Deception level) complex elements

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Poker Face" \- Advantage on Deception checks to maintain a lie  
Level 6: Unlock "False Identity" \- Create a persistent alter ego that's harder to see through (+3 to related Deception checks)  
Level 9: Unlock "Grand Deception" \- Once per week, automatically succeed on a Deception check

4\. Etiquette (INT):  
Description: Knowledge of proper social behavior in various settings.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Etiquette checks.  
\- Improves ability to navigate social situations and gain favor.

Formula:  
Etiquette Check: 1d12 \+ Etiquette \+ (INT / 2\) vs. DC  
Social Standing: Temporarily increase apparent social class by 1 per 3 levels of Etiquette

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Social Chameleon" \- Advantage on Etiquette checks in unfamiliar cultural settings  
Level 6: Unlock "Faux Pas Aversion" \- Once per day, reroll a failed Etiquette check  
Level 9: Unlock "Perfect Host/Guest" \- Gain a significant NPC contact after successfully navigating a major social event

5\. Leadership (SPI):  
Description: Inspiring and directing others.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Leadership checks.  
\- Improves ability to command groups and inspire allies.

Formula:  
Leadership Check: 1d12 \+ Leadership \+ (SPI / 2\) vs. DC  
Group Size: Can effectively lead a group of up to (Leadership level x 5\) individuals

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Rally" \- Once per day, grant allies within 30 feet a \+1 bonus to all checks for 1d4 rounds  
Level 6: Unlock "Inspire Greatness" \- Grant one ally advantage on their next check as a bonus action  
Level 9: Unlock "Legendary Commander" \- Once per week, automatically succeed on a Leadership check to command a large group

6\. Insight (SPI):  
Description: Reading people and discerning their motives.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Insight checks.  
\- Improves ability to detect lies and understand intentions.

Formula:  
Insight Check: 1d12 \+ Insight \+ (SPI / 2\) vs. Target's Deception DC  
Lie Detection: Sense basic truth/falsehood plus one subtle tell per 2 levels of Insight

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Gut Feeling" \- Once per day, gain advantage on an Insight check  
Level 6: Unlock "Cold Read" \- Make an Insight check as a free action once per social encounter  
Level 9: Unlock "Mind's Eye" \- Once per day, know if a creature within 30 feet is lying without making a check

## Mental Skills:

1\. Investigation (INT):  
Description: Gathering information through careful observation and deduction.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Investigation checks.  
\- Improves ability to find clues and solve puzzles.

Formula:  
Investigation Check: 1d12 \+ Investigation \+ (INT / 2\) vs. DC  
Clue Discovery: Find 1 \+ (Investigation level / 2\) clues per successful check

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Keen Eye" \- Advantage on Investigation checks to find hidden objects  
Level 6: Unlock "Rapid Analysis" \- Reduce time needed for thorough investigation by 25%  
Level 9: Unlock "Eureka Moment" \- Once per day, automatically succeed on an Investigation check

2\. Perception (SPI):  
Description: General awareness of surroundings and noticing details.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Perception checks.  
\- Improves ability to spot hidden things and avoid surprise.

Formula:  
Perception Check: 1d12 \+ Perception \+ (SPI / 2\) vs. DC  
Passive Perception: 10 \+ Perception skill \+ (SPI / 2\)

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Alertness" \- Cannot be surprised if conscious  
Level 6: Unlock "Danger Sense" \- Advantage on Perception checks to detect traps and ambushes  
Level 9: Unlock "Eagle Eye" \- Double your visual and auditory range

3\. Lore (INT):  
Description: Knowledge of history, legends, and cultures.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Lore checks.  
\- Improves recall of important information about the world.

Formula:  
Lore Check: 1d12 \+ Lore \+ (INT / 2\) vs. DC  
Knowledge Breadth: Can recall basic facts about (Lore level x 2\) different topics

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Savant" \- Choose a specialty; gain advantage on Lore checks in that area  
Level 6: Unlock "Obscure Knowledge" \- Once per day, recall an obscure fact that grants advantage on a related skill check  
Level 9: Unlock "Living Library" \- Can attempt Lore checks on any topic, even if untrained

4\. Arcana (INT):  
Description: Understanding of magic and magical phenomena.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Arcana checks.  
\- Improves ability to identify spells and magical effects.

Formula:  
Arcana Check: 1d12 \+ Arcana \+ (INT / 2\) vs. DC  
Spell Identification: Can identify spells of level (Arcana / 2, rounded up) or lower

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Magical Insight" \- Advantage on Arcana checks to identify magical items  
Level 6: Unlock "Counterspell" \- Once per day, attempt to counter a spell as a reaction  
Level 9: Unlock "Arcane Mastery" \- Can attempt to use magic items even if class restrictions aren't met

5\. Medicine (INT):  
Description: Knowledge of healing and treating injuries and illnesses.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Medicine checks.  
\- Improves healing effectiveness and disease treatment.

Formula:  
Medicine Check: 1d12 \+ Medicine \+ (INT / 2\) vs. DC  
Healing: Restore 1d4 \+ Medicine level HP per successful check

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Field Medic" \- Stabilize a dying creature as a bonus action  
Level 6: Unlock "Treat Disease" \- Advantage on checks to treat diseases and poisons  
Level 9: Unlock "Miraculous Recovery" \- Once per day, restore a creature to half HP as an action

6\. Nature (SPI):  
Description: Knowledge of plants, animals, and natural phenomena.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Nature checks.  
\- Improves survival skills and understanding of the natural world.

Formula:  
Nature Check: 1d12 \+ Nature \+ (SPI / 2\) vs. DC  
Foraging: Find enough food and water for (Nature level) people per day on a successful check

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Animal Whisperer" \- Advantage on checks to calm or influence animals  
Level 6: Unlock "Weather Sense" \- Accurately predict weather for the next 24 hours  
Level 9: Unlock "One with Nature" \- Can communicate simple ideas with plants and animals

7\. Engineering (INT):  
Description: Understanding and creating mechanical systems and structures.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Engineering checks.  
\- Improves ability to design, build, and repair constructions and devices.

Formula:  
Engineering Check: 1d12 \+ Engineering \+ (INT / 2\) vs. DC  
Construction Time: Reduce time to build or repair by 5% per Engineering level

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Quick Fix" \- Temporarily repair a device or structure as an action  
Level 6: Unlock "Improved Design" \- Create devices with 10% better performance than standard  
Level 9: Unlock "Master Engineer" \- Once per week, automatically succeed on an Engineering check

## Subterfuge Skills:

1\. Lockpicking (AGI):  
Description: Opening locks without the proper key.

\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Lockpicking checks.

Time Reduction: Reduce lockpicking time by 10% per level

\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Trap Handling checks.

Trap Handling Check: 1d12 \+ Trap Handling \+ (INT / 2\) vs. Trap DC  
Trap Complexity: Can handle traps of complexity equal to Trap Handling level

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Trap Sense" \- Advantage on saves against traps

4\. Disguise (INT):

Disguise Check: 1d12 \+ Disguise \+ (INT / 2\) vs. Observer's Perception DC

Level 6: Unlock "Method Actor" \- Advantage on social checks while in disguise

5\. Appraisal (INT):

Level 6: Unlock "Eye for Quality" \- Advantage on checks to detect fake or inferior goods  
Level 9: Unlock "Master Appraiser" \- Once per day, perfectly determine an item's value and properties

6\. Eavesdropping (SPI):  
Description: Listening in on conversations and detecting surveillance.  
Mechanics:  
\- Each level provides a \+1 bonus to Eavesdropping checks.

Listening Range: Clearly hear conversations up to (10 \+ 5 per Eavesdropping level) feet away

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Lip Reading" \- Understand speech by sight within 30 feet  
Level 6: Unlock "Selective Hearing" \- Filter out background noise for better clarity

## Magic Skills:

1\. Spellcasting (INT):  
Description: Proficiency in casting and controlling magic.  
Mechanics:  
\- Contributes to the Magical Attack Score.  
\- Improves overall spell effectiveness.

Formula:  
Magical Attack Score: (Base Score \+ INT \+ Spellcasting \+ Equipment Bonuses) / 2  
Magical Attack Roll: 1d12 \+ Magical Attack Score vs. 10 \+ target's SPI

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Spell Focus" \- \+1 to Magical Attack Score for one school of magic  
Level 6: Unlock "Mana Efficiency" \- Reduce MP cost of spells by 1 (minimum 1 MP)  
Level 9: Unlock "Arcane Mastery" \- Once per day, add full INT to Magical Attack Score for one spell

2\. Magical Defense (SPI):  
Description: Ability to resist and defend against magical attacks.  
Mechanics:  
\- Enhances magical defense.  
\- Improves resistance to magical effects.

Formula:  
Magical Defense: 10 \+ SPI \+ Magical Defense skill level

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Spell Resistance" \- \+2 to Magical Defense against one chosen school of magic  
Level 6: Unlock "Magical Barrier" \- Once per day, add your SPI to your Magical Defense for one round  
Level 9: Unlock "Spell Deflection" \- Once per day, on a successful defense, redirect a spell to a target within 30 feet

3\. Mana Control (INT):  
Description: Mastery over magical energy manipulation and conservation.  
Mechanics:  
\- Improves mana pool and regeneration.  
\- Enhances ability to manipulate magical energies.

Formula:  
Max MP: Base MP \+ (INT x 3\) \+ (Mana Control level x 2\)  
MP Regeneration: Recover (SPI \+ Mana Control level) MP per turn

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Mana Tap" \- Once per day, instantly recover INT \+ Mana Control level MP  
Level 6: Unlock "Efficient Casting" \- 10% chance to cast a spell without expending MP  
Level 9: Unlock "Mana Mastery" \- Once per day, all spells cost 1 MP for 1 minute

4\. Magical Knowledge (INT):  
Description: Understanding of magical theories, items, and phenomena.  
Mechanics:  
\- Improves ability to identify and understand magical effects.  
\- Enhances creation and use of magical items.

Formula:  
Magical Knowledge Check: 1d12 \+ INT \+ Magical Knowledge level vs. DC

Special:  
Level 3: Unlock "Spell Identification" \- Identify a spell being cast with a successful Magical Knowledge check  
Level 6: Unlock "Magical Insight" \- Create minor magical items or temporary enchantments  
Level 9: Unlock "Arcane Secrets" \- Once per week, attempt to create a major magical item

## Starting Gold Calculation

Starting GP \= (Base Class GP \+ Life Event Modifier) x 1d6

1\. Base Class GP:  
Peasant: 10gp | Laborer: 15gp | Urchin: 5gp  
Apprentice: 20gp | Militia: 25gp | Novice: 15gp

2\. Life Event Modifier:  
Severe Illness: \-5gp | Grueling Labor: \+5gp | Athletic Training: \+0gp  
Intense Study: \+10gp | Mystical Encounter: \+15gp | Childhood Trauma: \-10gp  
Adventurous Upbringing: \+5gp | Scholarly Pursuits: \+15gp | Peaceful Life: \+0gp  
Isolated Childhood: \-5gp | Military Training: \+10gp | Magical Awakening: \+20gp  
Parental Loss: \-5gp | Orphaned Young: \-10gp | Hard Labor: \+5gp  
Blessed with Health: \+5gp | Nimble Childhood: \+0gp | Farm Life: \+5gp  
Severe Injury: \-10gp | Early Mentorship: \+10gp | Harsh Environment: \-5gp  
Frequent Travel: \+5gp | Sickness Recovery: \+0gp | Rich Education: \+25gp  
Desert Life: \-5gp | Lonely Upbringing: \-5gp | Combat Training: \+10gp  
Regular Meditation: \+5gp | Nomadic Life: \+0gp | Repeated Trauma: \-15gp  
Street Smarts: \+5gp | High Society: \+30gp | Religious Upbringing: \+10gp  
War Survivor: \+0gp | Jungle Life: \-5gp | Early Loss of Family: \-10gp  
Forest Dweller: \+0gp | Wealthy Childhood: \+35gp | Harsh Winters: \-5gp

3\. Multiplier: Roll 1d6

Example: Militia (25gp) with Farm Life (+5gp) rolls 4 on 1d6  
Calculation: (25 \+ 5\) x 4 \= 120gp starting gold

Note: Minimum starting gold is 0gp (if calculation results in a negative number).

## Weapons and Equipment

Weapons:  
1\. Simple Weapons:  
Dagger (2gp): Small, concealable blade. Versatile for combat and utility.  
Club (1gp): Crude but effective. Favored by thugs and militia.  
Quarterstaff (2gp): Long wooden pole. Useful for walking and fighting.  
Sling (1gp): Leather pocket on a cord. Hurls stones with surprising force.  
Thrown Rock (free): Nature's weapon. Accuracy varies widely.

2\. Martial Weapons:  
Shortsword (10gp): Balanced blade. Ideal for swift, precise strikes.  
Longsword (15gp): Versatile weapon. Symbol of knighthood and valor.  
Greataxe (30gp): Massive chopping blade. Cleaves foes with brutal force.  
Warhammer (12gp): Weighty head on a sturdy haft. Crushes armor and bone.  
Spear (5gp): Long reach. Equally useful thrown or held.  
Battleaxe (10gp): Single-bladed axe. Vicious chopping power.  
Halberd (20gp): Axe-blade and spike on a long pole. Versatile polearm.

3\. Ranged Weapons:  
Shortbow (25gp): Compact bow. Deadly in skilled hands.  
Longbow (50gp): Tall bow with great range. Requires strength and practice.  
Light Crossbow (25gp): Mechanical bow. Powerful but slow to reload.  
Heavy Crossbow (50gp): Massive crossbow. Punches through armor at range.  
Throwing Axes (5gp each): Balanced for throwing. Favored by northern tribes.

Armor:  
1\. Light Armor:  
Padded (5gp, \+1 PD): Quilted layers. Better than nothing.  
Leather (10gp, \+2 PD): Hardened hide. Favored by scouts and thieves.  
Studded Leather (25gp, \+3 PD): Leather reinforced with metal studs. Flexible protection.

2\. Medium Armor:  
Hide (10gp, \+3 PD, \-1 AGI): Thick animal pelts. Crude but effective.  
Chain Shirt (50gp, \+4 PD, \-1 AGI): Interlocking metal rings. Noisy but protective.  
Scale Mail (50gp, \+5 PD, \-2 AGI): Overlapping metal scales. Solid defense at a cost to agility.

3\. Heavy Armor:  
Ringmail (30gp, \+5 PD, \-2 AGI, \-1 STR): Leather with sewn-on metal rings. Cheap but cumbersome.  
Chain Mail (75gp, \+6 PD, \-3 AGI, \-1 STR): Full body chain. Excellent protection, very noisy.  
Plate (200gp, \+8 PD, \-4 AGI, \-2 STR): Full plate armor. Ultimate protection at great cost.

4\. Shields:  
Buckler (5gp, \+1 PD): Small round shield. Allows use of off-hand.  
Shield (10gp, \+2 PD): Standard kite shield. Solid protection.  
Tower Shield (30gp, \+3 PD, \-1 AGI): Massive shield. Mobile wall at the cost of agility.

General Equipment:  
1\. Adventuring Gear:  
Backpack (2gp): Sturdy pack. Essential for any adventurer.  
Bedroll (1gp): Simple sleeping mat. Vital for rest on the road.  
Rope (50 ft, 1gp): Strong hemp rope. Countless uses.  
Torch (1gp): Simple light source. Burns for 1 hour.  
Lantern (5gp): Covered flame. Longer-lasting than a torch.  
Oil Flask (1gp): Fuel for lanterns. Also flammable.  
Flint and Steel (1gp): Fire starter. Reliable in all weather.  
Waterskin (1gp): Leather water container. Holds 4 pints.  
Rations (1 day, 1gp): Dried meat and fruit. Travels well.  
Tent (10gp): Canvas shelter. Sleeps 2 comfortably.

2\. Tools:  
Lockpicks (25gp): Delicate tools. For opening locks... legally, of course.  
Climbing Kit (25gp): Pitons, harness, etc. Essential for scaling walls.  
Healer's Kit (5gp): Bandages and salves. Helps stabilize the wounded.  
Herbalism Kit (5gp): For gathering and using herbs. Vital for natural remedies.  
Fishing Tackle (1gp): Rod, line, and hooks. For procuring dinner.  
Smith's Tools (20gp): Hammers, tongs, etc. For metalworking.  
Thieves' Tools (25gp): Lockpicks and more. A rogue's best friend.

3\. Containers and Miscellaneous:  
Pouch (1gp): Small bag. Holds coins and small items.  
Sack (1gp): Large cloth bag. Cheap carrying solution.  
Barrel (2gp): Wooden container. Holds 40 gallons.  
Chest (5gp): Sturdy box. Secures valuables.  
Holy Symbol (5gp): Divine focus. Channel the power of the gods.  
Spellbook (50gp): Arcane tome. A wizard's most prized possession.  
Ink and Quill (10gp): Writing implements. For spells or correspondence.  
Musical Instrument (25gp): Various types. Brings joy and coin.  
Disguise Kit (25gp): Makeup and props. Become someone else.  
Poison Vial (50gp): Toxic substance. Handle with extreme caution.

4\. Mounts and Vehicles:  
Horse (75gp): Sturdy steed. Faithful companion on long journeys.  
Donkey (8gp): Pack animal. Stubborn but reliable.  
Cart (15gp): Two-wheeled vehicle. Pulled by one animal.  
Wagon (35gp): Four-wheeled vehicle. For serious hauling.

5\. Trade Goods:  
Cloth (per sq. yard, 1gp): Woven fabric. Basis of many crafts.  
Wheat (per pound, 1gp): Staple grain. Feeds the masses.  
Chicken (2gp): Provides eggs and meat. Easy to raise.  
Cow (10gp): Provides milk and meat. Valuable livestock.  
Iron (per pound, 1gp): Raw metal. Basis of tools and weapons.

## Classes and progression {#classes-and-progression}

All characters start as one of the Base Classes, based on your starting attribute scores.  
Through accomplishing specific deeds, surviving dangerous situations, and accumulating experience, characters can progress to Intermediate Classes.  
Advancing to Advanced Classes requires not just experience, but also completing specific quests, gaining rare knowledge, or being recognized by powerful entities.  
Legendary Classes are the stuff of myths \- perhaps only one or two exist in all of Aventhar at any given time.

Tiers:  
1 (Starting): Peasant, Laborer, Urchin, Apprentice, Militia, Novice  
2 (Experienced): Footman, Scout, Thief, Acolyte, Hedge Wizard, Merchant  
3 (Skilled): Warrior, Ranger, Rogue, Priest, Mage, Bard  
4 (Expert): Knight, Hunter, Assassin, Cleric, Sorcerer, Diplomat  
5 (Master): Paladin, Beast Master, Shadowblade, High Priest, Archmage, Loremaster  
6 (Legendary): Eternal Champion, Primal Hunter, Shadow Walker, Avatar of the Gods, Ether Lord, World Shaper

Progression Requirements:

Tier 1 to 2:  
Footman: Survive 10 combats; Master 2 weapons; Complete military training  
Scout: Track 3 days; Survive wilderness week; Deliver crucial intel  
Thief: Pickpocket 20; Disarm 10 traps; Join thieves' guild  
Acolyte: 20 healing rituals; Divine vision; Convert 10 people  
Hedge Wizard: Cast 5 spells; Craft magic item; Survive magical mishap  
Merchant: 100 gold; 3 trade contacts; Complete major trade deal

Tier 2 to 3:  
Warrior: Win duel; Lead military op; Master 3 fighting styles  
Ranger: Solo dangerous beast; Map uncharted area; Bond with animal  
Rogue: Infiltrate guarded location; 500 gold heist; Establish informant network  
Priest: Public miracle; Establish temple; Defeat faith enemy  
Mage: Master 3 magic schools; Survive high Ether area; Decipher ancient text  
Bard: 1000 gold; Master instrument; Gather 5 cultural stories

Tier 3 to 4:  
Knight: Complete grand quest; Win tournament; Swear/uphold oath  
Hunter: Defeat legendary beast; Survive 5 extreme environments; Tame monster  
Assassin: Eliminate VIP; Create unique poison; Fake own death  
Cleric: Resurrect dead; Banish powerful entity; Receive divine mandate  
Sorcerer: 10 wild magic uses; Create new spell; Survive pure Ether contact  
Diplomat: Prevent war; Royal performance; Expose major conspiracy

Tier 4 to 5:  
Paladin: Lead campaign; Defeat legendary monster; Establish knight order  
Beast Master: Command legendary beasts; Thrive in deadliest environment; Solo defeat army with animals  
Shadowblade: Infiltrate secure fortress; Assassinate demon lord; Control throne from shadows  
High Priest: Become deity's voice; Banish god's avatar; Establish major religion  
Archmage: Control wild magic; Create major artifact; Establish magic school  
Loremaster: Broker nation peace; Uncover world-changing secret; Master 10 languages

Tier 5 to 6:  
Eternal Champion: Turn world war; Defeat Thar's avatar; Become greatest warrior  
Primal Hunter: Tame primordial beast; Shape-shift at will; Revive extinct species  
Shadow Walker: Perfect invisibility; Travel through shadows; Reshape continental politics unseen  
Avatar of the Gods: Ascend to demigod; Alter deity's domain; Win divine war  
Ether Lord: Reshape geography with magic; Create new plane; Achieve immortality  
World Shaper: Rewrite reality law; Uncover Aven/Thar's nature; Create new race

3\. Thief  
   \- Stat Requirements: AGI 12+, INT 10+

4\. Acolyte  
   \- Stat Requirements: SPI 12+, INT 10+

5\. Hedge Wizard
